column5: The 1920 exposure table is worked on a 50 per cent shutter opening (OCR). 50 per cent of a revolution is 180 deg, the same basis the 1927 edition gives. The two editions agree.

Editions differ on cost and magnification: 1920 gives an average of $2.00 a foot (50c to $5.00) and about 150 diameters on screen; 1927 gives $3.50 (range $1 to $10) and 250 diameters. Both are historical; quote neither as current.
Only the 1920 edition advises X-back film (gum-backed stock that stops static in cool weather, roughly September to May). The 1927 edition does not mention it.
